conversation.speaker: dialogue
conversation.text:
Police: Since when did Ms. Minyoung start going out to look for Xiyuan?
Respondent: Her condition suddenly worsened... It should have been because of the elementary school admission notice.
Respondent: In December last year, the subdistrict office sent a piece of mail. I usually open the mail in advance, afraid that there might be something Minyoung shouldn’t see.
Respondent: But when I opened this one and saw the words “admission notice,” it startled me... It was only then that I realized...
Respondent: They had never gone to register.
Respondent: I saw the registration date clearly written on it along with the child’s name... Just looking at it made me feel like I was going crazy... let alone the child’s mother...
Respondent: Oh... I’m sorry, Officer.
Respondent: As a sinner, how could I have the face to complain to you?
Respondent: I’m truly sorry...
Respondent: At that time, I panicked. I accidentally let Minyoung, who was beside me, see it as well.
Respondent: After she saw it, she showed a face full of happiness.
Respondent: I don’t even know how long it had been since I last saw her smile so happily.
Respondent: The registration date written on it was at the end of December. After seeing it, she kept urging me, saying we had to get the school uniform tailored before then.
Respondent: She also said that before school starts, vaccinations were needed and stationery had to be bought. Where has this child gone? Why hasn’t she come back yet?
Respondent: It was from that time on.
Respondent: From that time on, she went to the nearby amusement parks every day to look for Xiyuan.
